extracted.intended_audience: agency officials, administrative lawyers, judges, and policymakers involved in federal administrative procedure and judicial review
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements drawn from the Administrative Procedure Act (committee bill text and explanatory notes) governing agency rulemaking, adjudication, licensing, examinations, publication, and judicial review. Intended to guide agency behavior, agency decision records, and court reviewability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency review of examiners' decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may adopt in whole or part the findings, conclusions, and basis stated by examiners or other presiding officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the agency determines to review such a case, it should, so far as possible, specify the issues of law, fact, or discretion for review with particularity. Agency rules must prescribe a reasonable time for appeals from initial examiners' decisions. Examiner decisions become part of the record and are of consequence (e.g., credibility determinations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of intermediate recommended decision procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Where issues of fact are sharply controverted or the case or class of cases tends to become accusatory in nature, sound practice would require the agency to adopt the intermediate recommended decision procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The intermediate recommended decision is broadly drawn for rule-making or initial license determinations but should be used when factual disputes or accusatory characteristics make it appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to submit findings, exceptions, and supporting reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to each recommended, or other decision or review the parties must be given an opportunity to submit (1) proposed findings and conclusions or (2) exceptions to recommended decisions or other decisions being appealed or reviewed, and (3) supporting reasons for such findings, conclusions, or exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record must show the official rulings upon each such finding, conclusion, or exception presented. 'Supporting reasons' means briefs on the law and facts must be received and fully considered by every recommending, deciding, or reviewing officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions must state findings, conclusions, and reasons on all material issues
rubrics_metrics.description: All recommended or other decisions become a part of the record and must include (1) findings and conclusions, as well as the reasons or basis therefor, upon all the material issues of fact, law, or discretion presented by the record and (2) the appropriate agency action or denial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements of reasons may be long or short depending on the nature, novelty, or complexity of the issues, but must be sufficiently related to the record and law to advise the parties and any reviewing court of their record and legal basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receipt and consideration of briefs and oral argument
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Supporting reasons' means that briefs on the law and facts must be received and fully considered by every recommending, deciding, or reviewing officer. They must also hear such oral argument as may be required by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the issues are serious or the case becomes adversary in character, the agency should provide for oral argument before all recommending, deciding, or reviewing officers. The bill does not diminish rights to oral argument.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of stated reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement that the agency must state the reasons or basis for its findings and conclusions means that such findings and conclusions must be sufficiently related to the record and the law as to advise the parties and any reviewing court of their record and legal basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasoned opinions are the normal means; length varies with complexity. Findings must enable parties to determine what further facts they might offer on rehearing or reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Findings must cover credibility, law, fact, and discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Findings and conclusions must include all the relevant issues of law and fact presented by the record. Where oral testimony is in conflict or subject to doubt of its credibility, the credibility of witnesses would be a necessary finding if the facts are material. The relevant issues extend to matters of administrative discretion as well as of law and fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure of the basis for the exercise (or failure to exercise) discretion is important so parties can know what additional facts to offer on rehearing; agencies often err by addressing only whether they have power rather than how discretion should be exercised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and availability of decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: When made, decisions as defined by this section must be served on parties named, and also furnished to those participating as well as to interested persons who request them or have attempted to participate or intervene.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any person who requests in writing to be notified or given copies should have his request honored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on sanctions and powers (jurisdictional confinement)
rubrics_metrics.description: No sanction may be imposed or substantive rule or order be issued except within the jurisdiction delegated to the agency and as authorized by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may not undertake anything statutes or other adequate sources (treaties, etc.) do not authorize. Where sources are specific no additional authority may be assumed; where general, no authority beyond generality may be exercised. Agencies cannot exercise functions of other agencies; sanctions/relief must be identified and authorized and properly apply to the factual situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on use of publicity as penalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicity may in no case be utilized directly or indirectly as a penalty or punishment save as so authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legitimate publicity is the issuance of authorized documents (notices or decisions); apart from actual and final adjudication after all proceedings, no publicity should reflect adversely upon any person, organization, product, or commodity otherwise than as required to carry on authorized agency functions and necessary in administration. Agencies must not permit informational releases to be utilized as penalties or to the injury of parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promptness and 'reasonable dispatch' in licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required, with due regard for the rights or privileges of all interested parties or persons adversely affected, to proceed with reasonable dispatch to conclude and decide proceedings on applications for licenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requirement of dispatch means agencies must proceed as rapidly as is feasible and practicable rather than at their own convenience. Undue delays are subject to correction by mandatory injunction pursuant to section 10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity before revocation of licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: They are not to withdraw a license without first giving the licensee notice in writing and an opportunity to demonstrate or achieve compliance with all lawful requirements except in cases of willfulness or those in which public health, interest, or safety requires otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions to this requirement apply only where demonstrable facts fully and fairly warrant them; 'willfulness' must be manifest. The 'public ... interest' standard means clear and immediate necessity for due execution of laws; it does not permit ignoring notice and opportunity to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing-effect of licenses pending renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: In businesses of a continuing nature, no license expires until timely applications for new licenses or renewals are determined by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This operates whether or not a hearing is statutorily required; it does not confer licensing powers but limits when licenses lapse during administrative processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial review generally available except where statute precludes
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 10 on judicial review does not apply in any situation so far as there are involved matters with respect to which statutes preclude judicial review or agency action is by law committed to agency discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To preclude judicial review, a statute must on its face give clear and convincing evidence of intent to withhold review; mere failure to provide for review is not evidence of intent to withhold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matters of discretion versus questions of law
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters of discretion are necessarily exempted from the section, since otherwise courts would supersede agency functioning. But questions of law properly presented are not withdrawn from reviewing courts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where statutory standards or definitions require or deny action in given situations, the determination of facts does not lie in agency discretion but must be supported by the administrative or judicial record. Existence of discretion does not prevent a person from bringing review but may prevent him from prevailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to judicial review for 'legal wrong' or adverse statutory effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person suffering legal wrong because of any agency action, or adversely affected within the meaning of any statute, is entitled to judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 'Legal wrong' means an illegal effect as specified in section 10(e): the complainant must show the action is contrary to law in substance or procedure. Applicable law includes constitutional and all other applicable law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible forms of judicial action
rubrics_metrics.description: The technical form of proceeding for judicial review is any special proceeding provided by statute or, in the absence or inadequacy thereof, any relevant form of legal action (such as declaratory judgments or injunctions) in any court of competent jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency action is also subject to judicial review in any civil or criminal proceeding for enforcement except to the extent that prior, adequate, and exclusive opportunity for such review is provided by law. Declaratory judgment procedures may be operative before statutory forms are available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of reviewable agency acts
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency action made reviewable specially by statute or final agency action for which there is no other adequate judicial remedy is subject to judicial review. Preliminary or procedural matters not directly subject to review are reviewable upon the review of final actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except as statutes may expressly require otherwise, agency action is final for purposes of the section whether or not there has been presented or determined any application for declaratory order, reconsideration, or an appeal to superior agency authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and limits of 'final' agency action
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Final' action includes any effective or operative agency action for which there is no other adequate remedy in any court. Action which is automatically stayable on further proceedings invoked by a party is not final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconsideration includes reopening, rehearing, etc. Agencies may by rule require an appeal to superior agency authority before judicial review only if the administrative decision meanwhile is inoperative; otherwise such a requirement would force parties to continue to suffer the agency action without recourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary relief and preservation of status quo pending review
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending judicial review any agency may postpone the effective date of its action. Upon conditions and as may be necessary to prevent irreparable injury, any reviewing court may postpone the effective date of any agency action or preserve the status quo pending conclusion of review proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relief is equitable and should be used to prevent irreparable injury or afford parties an adequate judicial remedy. Such relief normally limited to complainant parties; courts should consider that third parties may be adversely affected and may require security from the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory grounds for holding agency action unlawful
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewing courts must hold unlawful any action, findings, or conclusions found to be (1) arbitrary or an abuse of discretion, (2) contrary to the Constitution, (3) contrary to statutes or statutory right, (4) without observance of procedure required by law, (5) unsupported by substantial evidence in any case reviewed upon the record of an agency hearing provided by statute, or (6) unwarranted by the facts insofar as the latter are subject to trial de novo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts must decide all relevant questions of law and interpret constitutional and statutory provisions. They are to consider the whole record (or parts cited) and must take due account of the rule of prejudicial error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whole record and prejudicial error considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: In making these determinations the court is to consider the whole record or such parts as any party may cite, and due account must be taken of the rule of prejudicial error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts may not look only to the case presented by one party since other evidence may weaken or destroy that case. A procedural omission cured prior to finality is not reversible error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and standard of 'substantial evidence'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Substantial evidence' means evidence which on the whole record is clearly substantial, plainly sufficient to support a finding or conclusion under the requirements of section 7(e), and material to the issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts must exercise independent judgment on the whole record to determine whether the evidence is sufficiently substantial to support agency findings, avoiding reliance on suspicion, surmise, implications, or incredible evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial de novo where administrative record inadequate
rubrics_metrics.description: The sixth category respecting establishment of facts upon trial de novo requires the reviewing court to determine the facts in any case of adjudication not subject to statutory agency hearing and record, or where facts are relevant to legal questions presented and no adequate administrative record exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where statutes do not provide that an agency shall make the record, the record must be made in court. Examples include tax assessments or agency orders not made after a statutory administrative hearing; courts may try facts in those enforcement or challenge proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment, tenure, and duties of examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to appoint such examiners as may be necessary for proceedings under sections 7 and 8, who are to be assigned to cases in rotation so far as practicable and to perform no inconsistent duties. They are removable only for good cause determined by the Civil Service Commission after opportunity for hearing and upon the record thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners are to receive compensation prescribed by the Commission independent of agency recommendations or ratings. One agency may, with consent, borrow examiners from another; assignment in rotation prevents disfavoring though specialization is permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications, independence, and compensation of examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: That examiners be 'qualified and competent' requires the Civil Service Commission to fix appropriate qualifications and the agencies to seek fit persons. The Commission must prescribe and adjust examiners' salaries independently of agency ratings and recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tenure and compensation provisions are designed to make examiners largely independent; salaries should be high enough to attract superior personnel. Commission may classify positions and reclassify examiners as experience and duties require.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil Service Commission review and protections for examiners
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission must afford any examiner an opportunity for a hearing before acceding to an agency request for removal, and even then its action would be subject to judicial review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hearing and decision would be made under sections 7 and 8 of the bill; this provides protections against arbitrary removal and preserves examiner independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction: constitutional rights and effect of invalid provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the bill is to diminish constitutional rights or limit or repeal additional requirements of law. The unconstitutionality of any portion or application of the bill is not to affect other portions or applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements of evidence and procedure apply equally to agencies and private persons except as otherwise provided by law. Agencies are granted authority necessary to comply with the bill.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective dates, deferred implementation, and 'initiated' proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill would become law three months after approval except that sections 7 and 8 take effect six months after approval, the requirements of section 11 become effective a year after approval, and no requirement is mandatory as to any agency proceeding initiated prior to the effective date of such requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The word 'initiated' means a proceeding formally begun as by issuance of a complaint or notice of a rule-making hearing. Deferred effective dates are intended to afford agencies time to prepare and adjust procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: No coerced waiver of bill's provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: No agreed waiver of its provisions would suffice, unless entirely voluntary and without any manner or form of coercion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Waivers must be truly voluntary; agencies cannot extract waivers that effectively strip protections from parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-judicial enforcement and sanctions for noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: For willful failure to comply, funds may be withheld or officers or employees may be subject to disciplinary action or dismissal. Judicial enforcement in case-by-case fashion is not the only method of enforcing the bill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although judicial review is indispensable, agencies themselves are the primary means of compliance; Congress and the people must look to agencies for fair administration; other administrative sanctions may be used to secure compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of covered terms (agency, rule, order, license, sanction, relief, agency proceeding/action)
rubrics_metrics.description: The bill provides detailed definitions: 'Agency', 'Person and party', 'Rule and rule making', 'Order and adjudication', 'License and licensing', 'Sanction and relief', and 'Agency proceeding and action' which determine the scope of coverage and obligations under the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions are essential to determine what processes and actions are subject to the Act's procedural and disclosure requirements; changes in wording (e.g., 'particular' as well as 'general' applicability) are intentional to avoid controversies over coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public information requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency shall separately state and currently publish in the Federal Register (1) descriptions of its central and field organization, including delegations of final authority and methods for the public to secure information or make submittals; (2) statements of the general course and method by which its rulemaking and adjudicating functions are channeled and determined, including nature and requirements of formal or informal procedures and forms/instructions; and (3) substantive rules, statements of general policy, or interpretations for guidance of the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No person shall be required to resort to organization or procedure not so published. Publication in the Federal Register ensures notice and accessibility of agency processes, forms, and substantive policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of opinions and orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency shall publish or, in accordance with published rule, make available to public inspection all final opinions or orders in the adjudication of cases (except those required for good cause to be held confidential and not cited as precedents) and all rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This promotes transparency and availability of precedential administrative decisions, subject to confidentiality exceptions for good cause.
